title: Keeping beer fresh
lead: Beer is a fresh product. Cold, dark and first in, first out.

sections.name: Fresh is best

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Most beer is at its best the day it leaves the brewery.

Bottles and cans: up to about 6 months cold; hoppy beers fade sooner.

video.title: How Long Does Craft Beer Stay Fresh?

read.bigIdea: Beer doesn’t get better on the shelf.
read.where: Almost every beer is ready to drink when it leaves the brewery and is best **fresh**. Cicerone’s guide: **unpasteurized draft** stays fresh about **45–60 days** cold, **pasteurized draft** about **90–120 days**. Cold bottles and cans can last up to about **6 months**, but **hoppy beers** like IPA can change in **3 months** even cold.
read.mixup: Wine can improve with age; most beer can’t. Only a few strong styles are meant for the cellar.
read.sayIt: That one’s brewed to drink fresh, and ours just came in.

video.title: Should Beer Be Stored Cold For Freshness? | exBEERiments

read.bigIdea: Cold beer stays fresh. Warm beer goes stale.
read.where: Cold storage is best for all beer. Cicerone notes that beer at about **72°F** ages up to **ten times faster** than at **38°F**, and storage above about **80°F** can ruin it quickly. Moving beer between cold and room temperature doesn’t hurt it by itself; the warm time is what ages it.
read.mixup: Taking a case out of the cooler for an hour doesn’t “skunk” it. Warm time makes it **stale**; light makes it **skunky**.

keyPoints.line: glass blocks most of the light.

read.bigIdea: Keep beer out of the light.
read.where: Sunlight, fluorescent and most **LED** light break down the bitter compounds from hops, and the pieces form the same kind of compound a **skunk** sprays (3-MBT). It can happen in **a couple of minutes**. **Brown** glass blocks most of the damaging light; **green** blocks very little and **clear** none. **Cans**, **kegs** and bottles in **closed cases** are fully protected.
read.mixup: Some clear-bottle beers use a special hop extract that resists skunking. Most green and clear bottles don’t.

video.title: Beer Store Tips: Reading Beer Date Stamps

keyPoints.line: or a ring in the neck: don’t serve it.

read.bigIdea: Sell the oldest first, and check every bottle.
read.where: Rotate stock **first in, first out**: put new beer behind old, check **date codes** and pull anything past its date. Codes can be a normal date, a **day-of-year** code or the brewery’s own. Before you open a bottle, look: **white flakes** or a **thin ring** at the liquid line in the neck mean old beer. **Bottle-conditioned** beers are stored **upright**.
read.mixup: A date code isn’t always a best-by date. Some are the day it was packaged.

sources: Cicerone, US Certified Beer Server Syllabus v6.0, 2024 (cicerone.org); Cicerone blog, “Off” Flavors in Beer: The Basics (cicerone.org); Craft Beer & Brewing, Dictionary: lightstruck (from The Oxford Companion to Beer). Checked Nov 8, 2026.
